speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions. To understand the full picture, where exactly is the pain located, and how long have these symptoms been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: That self-resolving knee pain and recent camping trip in Minnesota are concerning for Lyme disease, but your sexual history raises the possibility of disseminated gonococcal infection. Given your wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions, have you noticed if the lesions are tender or painful, and do they resemble pustules or petechiae?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: The lesions you describe as "painless violaceous vesiculopustular" are classic for disseminated gonococcal infection, and the severe wrist pain with swelling suggests septic arthritis. Given your recent camping trip and history of knee pain, could you confirm if you have noticed any eye redness, joint swelling elsewhere, or a rash that appeared on your trunk? speaker: Doctor
text: The normal readings do not alter the clinical picture; the painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions and tenosynovitis of your wrist are highly specific for disseminated gonococcal infection. DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection (DGI) causing septic arthritis of the left wrist and tenosynovitis.
